info.title: Ghana NIA AWOPA Baby Registration API
info.description:
The Ghana National Identification Authority's AWOPA service, which mints a Ghana Card PIN (national ID) for a newborn from the baby's details plus a vouching relative's card and photograph. It is a private government API: NIA publishes no developer portal, no machine spec and no reference docs, so this document is reverse-engineered from the OpenFn ghana-nia adaptor's source (its request path, headers, bundled JSON request schema and the sample request/response bodies in its mock server) and from openfn-mocker's ghana-nia plugin.

The adaptor reaches it with configuration.baseUrl plus configuration.merchantKey, sends the merchant key both as the NIa_merchantKey header and as a merchantKey field appended to the body, and exposes registerChild() plus generic get/post builders that can reach any path here.

servers.description: The host the adaptor's bundled mock targets, and the only base URL ever named for this service. Callers set it through configuration.baseUrl.

tags.name: Baby Registration
tags.description: Minting a newborn's Ghana Card PIN from a vouching relative.

post.summary: Register a newborn and mint a Ghana Card PIN
post.description: Submits the baby's details together with a vouching relative's Ghana Card PIN and photograph. NIA verifies the voucher and returns the PIN minted for the baby. This is what the adaptor's registerChild() calls; it sends content-type: application/json and an NIa_merchantKey header, and appends merchantKey to the body.

200.description: Registration saved; the minted PINs are returned

get.description: Returns the registrations minted for this merchant. Not documented by NIA and not wrapped by a named adaptor operation: recovered from OpenFn's ghana-nia mock, which models the reads a workflow can reach through the adaptor's generic get(). The response shape is unverified against the live service. (The adaptor's get() also throws client-side before issuing a request, because its shared request helper dereferences data.merchantKey before checking that a body was supplied.)

get.summary: Look up one registration by baby PIN
get.description: Returns a single registration by the Ghana Card PIN minted for the baby. Not documented by NIA and not wrapped by a named adaptor operation: recovered from OpenFn's ghana-nia mock, which models the reads a workflow can reach through the adaptor's generic get(). The response shape is unverified against the live service. (The adaptor's get() also throws client-side before issuing a request, because its shared request helper dereferences data.merchantKey before checking that a body was supplied.)

parameters.name: babyPin
parameters.description: The babyPin returned when the child was registered, e.g. GHA-000000000-1.

merchantKey.name: NIa_merchantKey
merchantKey.description: The NIA merchant key. Also appended to every JSON body as merchantKey.

BabyData.description: The newborn's details. Every value is sent as a string, including the numeric ones. Field names follow the adaptor's own request schema, typos included (timeOfbirth).

timeOfbirth.description: Time of birth, HH:MM. Spelled 'timeOfbirth' by the service.

placeOfBirth.description: Health facility or place where the baby was delivered.

noSiblingsInDelivery.description: Number of siblings delivered with the baby, as a string.

weightAtBirth.description: Birth weight in kilograms, as a string.

lightwaveETrackerID.description: The baby's record id in the Lightwave eTracker system.

birthCertificateNumber.description: Birth certificate number issued by the Births & Deaths Registry.

BabyRegistrationRequest.description: Registration payload. The adaptor's bundled request schema — generated from a single NIA sample, so its own required list is not a vendor statement — lists every field of babyData and personVouching plus merchantKey, which is why nothing is marked required here.

merchantKey.description: The NIA merchant key. The OpenFn adaptor appends it to every request body from configuration.merchantKey and rejects a body that already carries one.

ErrorResponse.description: Error envelope. NIA answers 404 rather than 4xx-by-meaning when verification fails, and the message carries the service's own misspelling of 'Verification'.

PersonVouching.description: The relative vouching for the newborn. NIA verifies this person's Ghana Card and photograph before minting the baby's PIN.

ghanaCardPIN.description: The voucher's existing Ghana Card PIN.

etrackerLightwaveID.description: The voucher's record id in the Lightwave eTracker system.

Registration.description: The identifiers NIA mints for a registered newborn and the relative who vouched for it.

babyPin.description: The Ghana Card PIN issued to the baby.

voucherPin.description: The Ghana Card PIN of the vouching relative.

etrackerLightwaveId.description: The Lightwave eTracker id echoed back from babyData.lightwaveETrackerID.

lightwaveEtrackerId.description: Second spelling of the eTracker id; null in every observed response.

RegistrationList.description: Response envelope carrying a list of registrations.

RegistrationResponse.description: Response envelope carrying one registration. The OpenFn adaptor puts this whole envelope on state.data.
